Accountable obligation owner.value: Product Compliance owns assembly of the CY bid package (PBP, BPT, actuarial certification, supporting documentation); benefit-design escalations go to the Chief Actuary and Regulatory Counsel

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — 42 CFR 422.101(a) and (b) (all Part A/B basic benefits furnished consistent with NCDs and LCDs) and 42 CFR 422.254(a) (bid must cover all basic benefits), re-read against the current eCFR text alongside the CY Final Rate Announcement and the CY Bid Instructions posted in HPMS

In-scope processes.value: Annual Medicare Advantage bid preparation for every MA contract (H-number) and plan benefit package: benefit design → PBP build → BPT pricing → actuarial certification → package assembly, ahead of the first-Monday-in-June bid deadline

In-scope systems.value: CMS HPMS Bid Submission module (PBP and BPT uploads) with the assembled package and version history mirrored in the internal regulatory filing record for the contract year

Compliance procedure documented.value: MA Bid Package Preparation Procedure — basic-benefit inventory against Medicare Parts A and B, NCD/LCD mapping, PBP-to-BPT reconciliation, actuarial certification routing, and the pre-submission validation run

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and the Chief Actuary; re-approved each contract year after the Advance Notice and Final Rate Announcement are published

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Bid package must be complete and locked before the CMS bid deadline of the first Monday in June for the following contract year; internal lock is set 10 business days earlier to allow HPMS validation reruns

Deadline reminders configured.value: Bid calendar alerts at Rate Announcement (first Monday in April), T-45, T-20 and T-10 business days to the first-Monday-in-June deadline, addressed to the Product Filing Specialist and the Chief Actuary

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Locked PBP and BPT files, benefit inventory, NCD/LCD mapping and the signed actuarial certification retained 10 years from the end of the contract year per 42 CFR 422.504(d)

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any basic benefit missing from the PBP, any PBP-to-BPT mismatch, and any unsupported cost-share is logged as a bid-package exception with owner and clearance date before the package is locked

Remediation sign-off captured.value: The Chief Actuary signs the certification only after every open bid-package exception is cleared and re-reconciled

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every plan benefit package submitted for the contract year across all MA contracts (H-numbers), including SNP and non-SNP PBPs and every segment

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on basic benefits — one Part A or Part B benefit category absent, or one cost-share exceeding original Medicare where the bid claims parity, is a fail; PBP-to-BPT reconciliation must tie to the dollar

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual (per bid cycle); the test runs once per contract year on the locked pre-submission package, with 100% coverage of basic-benefit categories and a sample of cost-share cells

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have built the PBP, priced the BPT or authored the actuarial certification for any sampled plan

Evidence location for test results.value: Contract-year bid assurance workpaper (population of PBPs, benefit-category matrix, reconciliation, exceptions) filed in the compliance evidence repository under the H-number and contract year

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Locked PBP/BPT exports, benefit inventory with 42 CFR 422.101(a)/(b) mapping, NCD/LCD references and the signed certification, producible for a CMS bid desk review or program audit within 3 business days

Regulator response path.value: CMS bid desk review questions arrive through HPMS to the contract's bid contacts; the Product Filing Specialist drafts, the Chief Actuary clears pricing answers and Regulatory Counsel clears any benefit-coverage admission before it is uploaded

checklist.step: Open the contract-year bid package and fix its scope
actions: In HPMS open Contract Management ▸ Contract Service Area and export the list of every active H-number, PBP id and segment approved to bid for the coming contract year.
Ask the Insurance Product Manager which PBPs are renewing, which are new, which are consolidating (crosswalk) and which are non-renewing, and record the answer per PBP id.
Open a bid package record in the internal regulatory filing register keyed <H-number>-<PBP id>-CY<year> and attach the service-area export.
Set the internal lock date at 10 business days before the CMS bid deadline (first Monday in June) and publish it to Actuarial and Product.
checklist.done: every H-number/PBP id in scope has a bid package record, a renewal disposition and a published internal lock date.

checklist.step: Pull the CMS Rate Announcement and the contract-year bid instructions
actions: Download the Final Rate Announcement published by CMS on the first Monday in April, plus the CY Bid Instructions, PBP instructions and BPT instructions from the HPMS ▸ Bid Submission ▸ Reference Materials page.

Extract the items that change the build: county-level benchmark rates, the applicable normalization and coding-intensity factors, the star-rating quality bonus percentages and the maximum out-of-pocket (MOOP) limits for the year.
Note every change from the prior contract year in a one-page delta memo and circulate it to Product, Pricing and Compliance.
File the dated PDFs in the bid package record so the build can be defended against the instructions that were actually in force.
checklist.done: the dated Rate Announcement and bid instructions are filed and a delta memo naming the benchmark, MOOP and factor changes has been circulated.

checklist.step: Build the Part A and Part B basic-benefit inventory
actions: List every Medicare Part A and Part B benefit category on its own row — inpatient acute, inpatient psychiatric, SNF, home health, hospice carve-out, outpatient hospital, physician and professional services, DME, prosthetics and orthotics, diagnostic tests and radiology, outpatient therapy, dialysis, ambulance, preventive services and Part B drugs.
Against each row record the corresponding PBP section and screen where the benefit is coded (for example PBP B-1 inpatient hospital acute, B-8 outpatient services, B-10 ambulance, B-14 preventive).
Mark hospice explicitly as excluded from the MA benefit and payable by original Medicare under 42 CFR 422.101(a), so it is not mis-coded as a plan benefit.
Send the inventory to the Product / Filing Actuary and Regulatory Counsel for confirmation that no category is missing before PBP data entry starts.
checklist.done: every Part A and Part B benefit category has an inventory row tied to a named PBP section, with hospice recorded as the original-Medicare carve-out.

checklist.step: Map each basic benefit to the governing national and local coverage rules
actions: For every inventory row, look up the applicable National Coverage Determination in the CMS Medicare Coverage Database and record the NCD number and title on the row.
For benefits governed locally, identify the Medicare Administrative Contractor for each state in the service area and record the LCD number and its effective date.

Flag any benefit where the plan intends to apply a coverage criterion narrower than the NCD/LCD and route it to Regulatory Counsel — 42 CFR 422.101(b) does not permit the plan to be more restrictive than original Medicare.
Attach the coverage-rule map to the bid package record and name the clinical reviewer and date on it.
checklist.done: each basic benefit row carries an NCD or MAC-specific LCD reference and any narrower plan criterion is flagged to counsel.

checklist.step: Enter the benefit design into the Plan Benefit Package
actions: In the HPMS PBP software open the CY PBP for the H-number and PBP id and complete Sections A (plan level), B (Medicare-covered benefits), C (supplemental), C-Rx if applicable and D (out-of-pocket).
Enter the member cost share for every Section B service category — copay or coinsurance, deductible applicability, day ranges for inpatient and SNF, and the in-network and combined MOOP.
Compare each entered cost share to the original-Medicare equivalent and flag any cell where the plan share exceeds it for actuarial-equivalence support.
Run the PBP built-in error and warning report and clear every hard error before saving the version.
checklist.done: the PBP is complete for Sections A through D with no unresolved hard errors and every cost-share cell populated.

checklist.step: Price the bid in the Bid Pricing Tool
actions: Load the projected membership, risk score, allowed cost and utilization by service category from the pricing model into BPT Worksheet 1 (projected allowed costs) and the plan-level assumptions.

Complete BPT Worksheets 2 through 4 — non-benefit expense, gain/loss margin, and the A/B benefit and supplemental benefit split — using the base period experience period defined in the bid instructions.
Enter the county benchmark, quality bonus percentage and rebate allocation from the Rate Announcement and confirm the resulting standardized bid and rebate dollars.
Save the BPT with a version number and record in the bid package the model run id and the experience period end date behind each worksheet.
checklist.done: the BPT is complete for all worksheets, tied to a named pricing model run and experience period, and produces a standardized bid and rebate allocation.

checklist.step: Reconcile the PBP benefit design to the BPT pricing cell by cell
actions: Export the PBP cost-share grid and the BPT Worksheet 1 service-category grid into a single reconciliation workbook.
Match each PBP Section B service category to its BPT service category and compare the coded copay/coinsurance to the cost share priced.
Prove the MOOP entered in PBP Section D equals the MOOP modelled in the BPT and sits at or below the CMS mandatory limit for the contract year.
List every difference as a reconciliation item with an owner and clear each one by correcting the PBP or the BPT — never by annotating the difference.
checklist.done: the PBP and BPT reconcile with zero unexplained differences and the MOOP agrees across both and to the CMS limit.

checklist.step: Draft and route the actuarial certification
actions: Draft the certification required with the bid, stating that the bid reflects all basic benefits required by 42 CFR 422.254(a) and that the assumptions are reasonable and consistent with the CY bid instructions.

Attach the supporting documentation the instructions demand: base period experience, trend derivation, risk score projection, morbidity and benefit-change adjustments, and the non-benefit expense build.
Review the reconciliation workbook and the basic-benefit inventory before signing, and confirm no exception remains open in the tracker.
Sign, date and load the certification into the bid package record as a locked PDF.
checklist.done: a signed and dated actuarial certification citing 42 CFR 422.254(a) is filed with its full supporting documentation set.

checklist.step: Assemble the supporting documentation upload set
actions: Build the upload set the bid instructions require per PBP: BPT file, PBP file, actuarial certification, supporting documentation workbook and any benefit-specific attachments.
Name every file to the CMS convention <contract>_<PBP>_<document type>_CY<year> and confirm each opens, is text-searchable and is inside the HPMS upload size limit.
Cross-check the set against the CY bid instructions submission checklist item by item and initial each line.
Store the set in the document repository under the bid package record with version control switched on.
checklist.done: the upload set is complete against the CMS submission checklist, correctly named and version-controlled.

checklist.step: Complete the CMS bid attestations and contact data
actions: In HPMS open Contract Management ▸ Contact Management and confirm the bid, actuarial and compliance contacts are current, with working phone and email for the desk review window.
Complete the contract-year attestations required alongside the bid, including the service area, network adequacy and benefit attestations tied to the H-number.
Confirm each attestation is executed by an individual with signature authority recorded in the HPMS user role for the contract.
Screenshot each completed attestation screen into the bid package record.
checklist.done: bid contacts are current and every contract-year attestation is executed by an authorised signatory with a captured screen.

checklist.step: Have Regulatory Counsel clear the benefit language and coverage positions
actions: Read the benefit descriptions that will flow from the PBP into the Evidence of Coverage and Summary of Benefits and check none narrows a Part A or Part B benefit.
Rule on every criterion flagged as narrower than an NCD or LCD, and either strike it or document the CMS-permitted basis for it under 42 CFR 422.101(b).
Confirm that hospice is described as covered by original Medicare and not by the plan.
Record the clearance with counsel name, date and the version of the PBP reviewed.
checklist.done: counsel has cleared the benefit language with a dated note against a named PBP version and no unresolved narrower-than-Medicare criterion remains.

checklist.step: Add the SNP-specific components where the PBP is a special needs plan
actions: For each SNP PBP confirm the target population type (C-SNP, D-SNP or I-SNP) and complete the SNP-specific PBP screens for eligibility and target condition.
Attach the current NCQA Model of Care approval letter and its approval term (1, 2 or 3 years) and confirm it covers the contract year being bid.
Where the approval term expires before or during the contract year, open a resubmission task with the Medical / Nurse Case Manager against the NCQA submission window.
Record the MOC score and approval end date on the bid package record.
checklist.done: every SNP PBP has a matching NCQA MOC approval that covers the bid contract year, or a resubmission task with an owner and date.

checklist.step: Run the pre-submission validation and clear every error
actions: Upload the PBP and BPT into the HPMS bid submission validation and run the CMS edit checks for the contract year.
Export the error and warning report and assign each hard error to the PBP builder or the pricing actuary with a same-day clearance target.
Re-run the validation after each correction and keep the report from the final clean run as evidence.
Write a short note against each warning that is being accepted, naming who accepted it.
checklist.done: a final validation run shows zero hard errors and every accepted warning has a named acceptor.

checklist.step: Take the package through bid governance sign-off
actions: Convene the bid review committee no later than 10 business days before the first-Monday-in-June deadline with Actuarial, Product, Compliance and Legal present.
Walk the basic-benefit inventory, the reconciliation result, the validation report and the open exception list; refuse sign-off while any basic-benefit gap is open.
Record the decision per PBP id — approve to submit, approve with condition, or hold — with the condition owner and date.
Minute the meeting and file the minutes in the bid package record.
checklist.done: each PBP id carries a minuted committee decision and no PBP is approved with an open basic-benefit gap.

checklist.step: Lock the package and place it under the 10-year retention rule
actions: Freeze the approved PBP and BPT versions, the certification, the inventory, the coverage map, the reconciliation and the validation report as a single immutable bid package.
Apply the 10-year retention label required by 42 CFR 422.504(d), counted from the end of the contract year being bid.
Index the package so it is retrievable by H-number, PBP id, contract year and document type.
Confirm write access is removed and only read and export remain for the bid contacts.
checklist.done: the locked bid package is stored read-only, labelled for 10-year retention and retrievable by H-number and PBP id.

testing.step: Build the population of plan benefit packages submitted for the contract year
actions: Export from HPMS Contract Management every H-number, PBP id and segment with a bid recorded for the contract year, including SNP and non-SNP plans.
Add plans that were crosswalked or consolidated so a renewing benefit design cannot escape the population.
Reconcile the count to the internal bid package register and resolve any difference before sampling.
Sign the population as complete with the extract date and the extractor's name.
testing.done: the population of PBPs is reconciled between HPMS and the internal register and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile every PBP to a locked package with a signed certification
actions: Match each population row to a bid package record on H-number + PBP id + contract year.
Confirm the package holds a locked PBP file, a locked BPT file and a signed, dated actuarial certification.
Check the certification date is on or before the submission date and after the final validation run.
List any PBP with a missing certification, an unsigned certification or a certification pre-dating the final package as an automatic exception.
testing.done: every PBP maps to a locked package whose certification is signed and correctly sequenced, or is listed as an exception.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of PBPs and cost-share cells
actions: Take 100% of SNP PBPs and 100% of newly launched PBPs.
Add a seeded random selection of 10 renewing PBPs, minimum 20 PBPs in total.
Within each sampled PBP, select 15 Section B cost-share cells at random plus the MOOP and the inpatient day-range cells as mandatory items.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all SNP and new PBPs, and names the mandatory cells tested in each.

testing.step: Re-perform the basic-benefit completeness check independently
actions: Build your own Part A and Part B benefit category list from the current Medicare benefit categories, without opening the team's inventory.
Open each sampled PBP in the HPMS PBP viewer and confirm every category is coded in the relevant Section B screen.
Treat a category absent from the PBP as a failure against 42 CFR 422.101(a) regardless of whether the team's inventory listed it.
Confirm hospice is not coded as a plan benefit and appears as the original-Medicare carve-out.
testing.done: each sampled PBP has been independently proved to code every Part A and Part B benefit category, with hospice correctly excluded.

testing.step: Re-perform the coverage-rule check against the Medicare Coverage Database
actions: For 10 sampled benefit rows, look the benefit up yourself in the CMS Medicare Coverage Database and read the current NCD and the MAC's LCD for a service-area state.
Compare the plan's coded coverage criterion to the NCD/LCD wording and mark any criterion that is narrower than original Medicare.
Confirm every narrower criterion carries a dated Regulatory Counsel clearance in the bid package.
Capture the coverage database screen you relied on into the workpaper with its retrieval date.
testing.done: no sampled benefit is more restrictive than its NCD/LCD without a dated counsel clearance, and each check has a captured source page.

testing.step: Trace sampled cost shares from the PBP through to the BPT
actions: For each sampled cost-share cell, read the value from the locked PBP export and find the matching BPT Worksheet 1 service category.
Confirm the priced cost share equals the coded cost share and that the same day ranges and deductible applicability were used.
Re-add the BPT service-category costs and prove they roll to the standardized bid shown on the BPT summary.
Record any difference in dollars, not as a narrative.
testing.done: every sampled cost-share cell ties from PBP to BPT and the service-category totals roll to the standardized bid.

testing.step: Recompute the MOOP and the submission-deadline maths
actions: Read the mandatory and voluntary MOOP limits from the CY Final Rate Announcement and compare them to the MOOP coded in each sampled PBP.
Recompute the in-network and combined MOOP against the priced cost shares and confirm neither exceeds the CMS limit.
Recompute the deadline: confirm the internal lock date sat at least 10 business days before the first Monday in June and that the submission timestamp pre-dates the CMS deadline.
Any MOOP above the limit or any submission after the deadline is a reportable breach, not a test exception.
testing.done: MOOP values sit within the CMS limit for every sampled PBP and the submission timestamps pre-date the first-Monday-in-June deadline.

testing.step: Test the SNP Model of Care evidence behind the sampled SNP bids
actions: Pull the NCQA MOC approval letter for each sampled SNP PBP and read the score and the approval term end date.
Confirm the approval covers the full contract year bid and matches the SNP type coded in the PBP.
Where the term expires during the contract year, confirm a resubmission task exists with an owner and a date inside the NCQA window.
Treat an expired or mismatched MOC approval as a fail against 42 CFR 422.101(f).
testing.done: every sampled SNP PBP has an in-force NCQA MOC approval matching its SNP type, or a dated resubmission task.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception with H-number, PBP id, the benefit or cell affected and the CMS citation breached.
Assign a root cause from the standard set — inventory gap, stale coverage rule, PBP data-entry error, BPT mapping error, late certification — and an owner.
Set a remediation date inside the bid desk review window so corrections can still be made through HPMS before bid finalisation.
Carry every open exception into next contract year's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has a tracker issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date inside the desk review window and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate by PBP and by cost-share cell and compare to the zero-tolerance basic-benefit threshold.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with the workpaper references behind it.
Have the Internal Auditor, who built no sampled PBP and priced no sampled bid, sign the workpaper.
Report the result and any basic-benefit breach to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the signed workpaper under the contract year.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and committee reporting date is filed in the evidence repository.

checklist.step: Confirm HPMS access and submission roles before the window opens
actions: In HPMS open User Management and confirm each named submitter holds an active CMS IDM account with the Bid Submission role for the correct H-number.
Ask the IT Service Desk to resolve any expired IDM credential or multi-factor enrolment at least 15 business days before the first-Monday-in-June deadline.
Confirm at least two submitters per contract so a single absence cannot block the upload.
Record the submitter names, IDM ids and role effective dates in the internal filing register.
checklist.done: at least two credentialed submitters per H-number hold the HPMS bid submission role and are recorded in the register.

checklist.step: Perform the upload dress rehearsal against the HPMS test window
actions: Use the HPMS bid test upload window CMS opens ahead of the deadline to upload the current PBP and BPT files for one representative contract.
Read the validation output and list every hard error and warning by PBP id with the owner who must clear it.
Time the upload end to end and record how long a full-portfolio submission takes so the deadline plan is based on measured, not assumed, duration.
File the test validation report in the bid package record.
checklist.done: a rehearsal upload has been completed, its errors assigned, and a measured full-portfolio upload duration is recorded.

checklist.step: Upload the bid files to HPMS in the required sequence
actions: In HPMS open Bid Submission ▸ Upload and select the contract year, H-number and PBP id.
Upload the PBP file first, then the BPT, then the supporting documentation and the actuarial certification, following the sequence in the CY bid submission instructions.
Wait for each upload to return an accepted status before starting the next; do not queue uploads over an unresolved rejection.
Repeat for every PBP id and segment in the portfolio, working from the largest membership downwards so the highest-exposure plans land first.
checklist.done: every PBP id shows an accepted upload for the PBP, BPT, supporting documentation and certification.

checklist.step: Capture the submission receipt and timestamp for every upload
actions: Open HPMS Bid Submission ▸ Submission Status and read the submission id, file name, submitter and CMS timestamp for each accepted upload.
Export or screenshot the status screen per PBP id and name the file <H-number>_<PBP>_submission-receipt_CY<year>.
Write the submission id and timestamp onto the internal register row for that PBP.
Confirm every timestamp pre-dates the first-Monday-in-June deadline and flag any that does not for immediate escalation.
checklist.done: each PBP row carries an HPMS submission id, a captured receipt and a timestamp proved to pre-date the CMS deadline.

checklist.step: Clear any rejection and re-upload before the deadline
actions: For every rejected upload, read the HPMS rejection reason code and text and copy it verbatim onto the register row.
Route file-content rejections to the Product / Filing Actuary and format or naming rejections to the Business Systems Analyst with a same-day fix target.
Re-upload the corrected file, capture the new submission id, and keep both the rejection and the successful receipt in the record.
Escalate to the Head of Compliance any rejection still open 48 hours before the deadline.
checklist.done: no rejection is left open, each has a verbatim reason, an owner and a successful re-upload receipt.

checklist.step: Open the disposition tracker for each submitted PBP
actions: Create one tracker row per H-number and PBP id with fields: submission id, submission date, current CMS status, assigned CMS account manager, open question count and next action date.
Set the status vocabulary to the CMS stages actually used — Submitted, In desk review, Question outstanding, Resubmission required, Approved, Rejected.
Link each row to its bid package record and its submission receipt.
Publish a daily status view to Product, Actuarial and Compliance for the duration of the desk review window.
checklist.done: every submitted PBP has a live disposition row with a CMS status, an account manager and a next action date.

checklist.step: Monitor HPMS memos and the desk review inbox daily
actions: Check the HPMS memo inbox and the bid contacts' mailboxes each business morning through the June-to-August desk review period.
Log every CMS question the same day with the question text, the PBP id it targets, the CMS response deadline and the internal owner.
Set the internal response target at one business day inside the CMS window so the answer can be cleared before it is sent.
Escalate to the Compliance Officer any question whose window is under 48 hours.
checklist.done: every CMS memo and desk review question is logged the day it arrives with a deadline and a named internal owner.

checklist.step: Draft, clear and upload each desk review response
actions: Draft the response against the exact question asked, citing the BPT worksheet, PBP screen or supporting documentation page that answers it.
Have the Chief Actuary clear any pricing or assumption answer and Regulatory Counsel clear any answer that concedes a benefit or compliance gap.
Upload the cleared response through the HPMS desk review thread for that submission id and capture the confirmation.
Update the tracker row with the response date, the clearer's name and the remaining open question count.
checklist.done: each question has a cleared, uploaded response with a captured HPMS confirmation and a tracker update.

checklist.step: Submit the compliance-program artefacts CMS expects alongside the contract
actions: Assemble the seven-element evidence set required by 42 CFR 422.503(b)(4)(vi): written standards of conduct and policies, the named compliance officer and compliance committee charter, training records, communication channels including the anonymous hotline, monitoring and auditing work plan, disciplinary standards, and the detected-offence response log.
Attach the annual utilization management committee record required by 42 CFR 422.137(d), showing the committee reviewed each prior authorization policy and the clinical basis for it.
Attach the prior authorization and continuity-of-care controls evidencing 42 CFR 422.138, including the 90-day continuity period for new enrollees.
Index the set to the contract year so it can be produced without reassembly during a CMS program audit.
checklist.done: a single indexed compliance-program evidence set covering all seven elements plus the UM committee and prior-authorization records exists for the contract year.

checklist.step: Track bid negotiation and any CMS-required resubmission
actions: Where CMS requires a bid change, record what CMS asked to change, the PBP or BPT cell affected and the CMS instruction reference.
Rebuild the affected file, re-run the PBP and BPT reconciliation and obtain a refreshed actuarial certification if the certified figures moved.
Re-upload through HPMS in the resubmission window CMS states, capture the new submission id and mark the superseded submission id as replaced.
Keep both versions so the change history from original bid to approved bid is readable end to end.
checklist.done: every CMS-required change has a rebuilt file, a refreshed certification where figures moved, a new submission id and a readable version history.

checklist.step: Record the CMS bid approval and the plan-level outcome
actions: Download the CMS bid approval notification from HPMS when CMS releases approvals ahead of the annual enrollment period.
Record per PBP id the approval date, the approved standardized bid, the rebate allocation and the star-rating-driven quality bonus applied.
Compare the approved figures to the submitted figures and record any CMS adjustment with its reason.
Move the tracker row status to Approved and notify Product, Marketing and Finance the same day.
checklist.done: every PBP id shows an approval date, the approved bid and rebate figures, and any CMS adjustment with its reason.

checklist.step: Execute the contract-year attestations and contract signature
actions: Read the contract-year MA contract and addenda CMS posts in HPMS Contract Management and identify any changed obligation from the prior year.
Confirm the signatory holds delegated authority recorded in the corporate authority matrix before executing.
Execute the contract inside the CMS-stated signature window and capture the executed copy and the HPMS confirmation.
Circulate a one-page note of the changed obligations to Compliance, Operations and Product.
checklist.done: the contract-year MA contract is executed inside the CMS window by an authorised signatory, with the changed obligations circulated.

checklist.step: Close every open item before the desk review window ends
actions: Run the tracker filtered to Question outstanding or Resubmission required and confirm the count is zero before the window closes.
For any item still open, escalate to the CMS account manager in writing and record the escalation date and CMS reply.
Confirm every response date sits inside the CMS-stated window and log any that does not as a submission exception with the day count missed.
Report the closing position per H-number to the bid review committee.
checklist.done: no HPMS question or resubmission remains open and every late response is logged with its day count.

checklist.step: Feed submission performance into the compliance monitoring work plan
actions: Summarise the cycle: uploads made, rejections, questions received, average response days and any missed window.
Add each recurring root cause as a monitoring activity in the compliance work plan required by 42 CFR 422.503(b)(4)(vi)(F).
Set the monitoring frequency and the owner and link it to the exception issues that generated it.
Present the summary to the compliance committee with the corrective actions proposed.
checklist.done: the cycle summary is presented and every recurring root cause has a dated monitoring activity with an owner in the work plan.

checklist.step: Archive the submission record under the 10-year retention rule
actions: Assemble the submission log, every HPMS receipt, the full desk review question-and-answer thread, the approval notice and the executed contract into one contract-year record.
Apply the 10-year retention label required by 42 CFR 422.504(d), counted from the end of the contract year.
Index by H-number, PBP id, submission id and CMS response date.
Remove write access and verify a test retrieval by submission id returns the complete thread.
checklist.done: the contract-year submission record is archived read-only, labelled for 10 years and retrievable by submission id.

testing.step: Build the population of HPMS submissions for the contract year
actions: Export from HPMS Bid Submission ▸ Submission Status every submission id recorded for the contract year across all H-numbers, including rejected and superseded uploads.
Add every desk review thread and every resubmission so corrections cannot fall out of scope.
Reconcile the export to the internal disposition tracker and investigate any submission present in one and absent from the other.
Sign the population as complete with the extract date and extractor name.
testing.done: the submission population is reconciled between HPMS and the internal tracker and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile every submitted PBP to a captured receipt
actions: Match each population row to a stored submission receipt on submission id.
Confirm the receipt shows the same H-number, PBP id, file name and CMS timestamp as the tracker row.
List any submission with no receipt, a receipt for a different file, or a timestamp that disagrees with the tracker as an automatic exception.
Confirm no accepted submission exists in HPMS that has no tracker row at all.
testing.done: every submission ties to a matching captured receipt, or is listed as an exception.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of submissions and desk review threads
actions: Take 100% of rejected uploads, 100% of resubmissions and 100% of desk review threads.
Add a seeded random selection of 15 clean first-time uploads, minimum 30 items in total.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
State which items are mandatory coverage and which are random so the basis of the sample is readable.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all rejections, resubmissions and question threads, and its basis is documented.

testing.step: Re-perform the deadline check in HPMS for each sampled submission
actions: Open HPMS Submission Status for each sampled submission id and read the CMS timestamp directly rather than trusting the tracker.
Compare it to the first-Monday-in-June deadline for the contract year and compute the margin in hours.
Where a resubmission followed, confirm it landed inside the window CMS stated in the memo requiring it.
Capture the HPMS status screen into the workpaper with the retrieval date.
testing.done: each sampled submission has an independently read CMS timestamp, a computed deadline margin and a captured source screen.

testing.step: Recompute the desk review response timing
actions: For each sampled desk review thread, read the CMS question date and the CMS-stated response window from the memo text.
Read the actual upload date of the response and recompute elapsed business days, excluding federal holidays.
Compare the elapsed count to the stated window and mark any overrun with the number of days missed.
Check the same recomputation against the 30-day corrective-action and 60-day reconsideration windows referenced by the obligation where those applied.
testing.done: every sampled thread has a recomputed business-day response time compared to the CMS window, with overruns quantified.

testing.step: Test that responses were cleared by the right authority before upload
actions: Pull each sampled response and identify whether it contains pricing content, benefit content or an admission of non-compliance.
Confirm pricing answers carry a Chief Actuary clearance and admissions carry a counsel clearance, both dated before the upload timestamp.
Treat a response uploaded before its clearance date as a control failure regardless of the answer's accuracy.
Record the clearer name and date against each sampled response in the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled response has a dated clearance from the right authority that pre-dates its upload.

testing.step: Trace the compliance-program evidence set to the seven required elements
actions: Open the contract-year evidence set and test one artefact against each element of 42 CFR 422.503(b)(4)(vi) — standards, officer and committee, training, communication, monitoring and auditing, discipline, and response to detected offences.
Confirm the compliance committee charter names its members and shows meeting dates inside the contract year.
Confirm the training records show completion for the population required, with dates inside the year.
Mark any element evidenced only by a policy document with no operating record as a fail.
testing.done: each of the seven elements is evidenced by a dated operating record, not a policy alone, or the gap is logged.

testing.step: Verify the utilization management committee and prior-authorization records
actions: Read the annual utilization management committee minutes and confirm the committee reviewed each prior authorization policy in force, as 42 CFR 422.137(d) requires.
Select 5 prior authorization policies and confirm each records the clinical evidence relied on and the reviewer who approved it.
Confirm the continuity-of-care control under 42 CFR 422.138 honours an active course of treatment for new enrollees for the minimum 90-day period.
Log any policy in force with no committee review inside the year as a fail.
testing.done: every in-force prior authorization policy shows an annual UM committee review with clinical basis, and continuity of care is evidenced.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception recording H-number, submission id, the window missed and the day count.
Assign a root cause from the standard set — credential lapse, file rejection not cleared, question logged late, clearance bottleneck, memo missed — and an owner.
Set a remediation date before the next bid cycle opens and link the issue to the compliance monitoring work plan activity that will retest it.
Escalate any missed CMS deadline to the Head of Compliance within one business day of discovery.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a quantified miss, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a linked monitoring activity.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report the test
actions: Compute the on-time submission rate and the on-time desk review response rate and compare both to the zero-tolerance threshold.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with the workpaper references behind it.
Have the Internal Auditor, who made and cleared none of the sampled submissions, sign the workpaper.
Report to the compliance committee and file the signed workpaper under the H-number and contract year.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the on-time rates, the conclusion and the committee reporting date and is filed in the repository.

checklist.step: Define the contract-year gate and the dates it enforces
actions: Open a release record per H-number and PBP id for the contract year and add four gate flags: bid approved, marketing cleared, October 1 marketing date, October 15 enrollment date.
Populate the fixed CMS dates for the year — marketing from October 1, annual enrollment October 15 to December 7, benefits effective January 1.
Set every flag to blocked by default so release is an explicit act rather than the absence of an objection.
Publish the gate definition to Marketing, Sales, Product Operations and the contact centre.
checklist.done: each PBP id has a release record with four blocked gate flags and the CMS dates populated and published.

checklist.step: Confirm CMS bid approval before any plan-specific communication
actions: Open HPMS Contract Management and read the bid approval status and date for each H-number and PBP id.
Record the approved benefit and premium values and compare them to the values Marketing intends to advertise.
Release the bid-approved flag only where HPMS shows an approval and the advertised values equal the approved values.
Notify Marketing in writing that plan-specific benefit and premium claims may now be drafted, naming the approval date.
checklist.done: the bid-approved flag is released only against an HPMS approval date and advertised values that equal approved values.

checklist.step: Classify each marketing material by its CMS review route
actions: List every material for the contract year — Summary of Benefits, Annual Notice of Change, Evidence of Coverage, enrollment forms, direct mail, television and radio scripts, web pages, agent scripts and third-party marketing organisation materials.
Classify each as requiring standard CMS review, eligible for the 5-day File-and-Use route, or a model or standardised document that must be used as CMS wrote it.
Record the classification basis against the CY marketing requirements section that grants the route.
Send the classification list to Regulatory Counsel for confirmation before submission starts.
checklist.done: every material carries a review-route classification with a cited basis, confirmed by counsel.

checklist.step: Submit materials to CMS and capture the Material ID
actions: In HPMS open the Marketing Review Module ▸ Material Submission, select the contract year and the H-number, and upload the material with its material type code.
Record the HPMS Material ID, the submission date and the review route selected on the material register row.
Attach the exact file submitted so the distributed version can later be proved identical to the reviewed version.
Confirm the material type code selected matches the classification agreed with counsel.
checklist.done: every material has an HPMS Material ID, a submission date, a stored submitted file and a matching material type code.

checklist.step: Compute and hold the review or File-and-Use period
actions: For standard-review materials compute the earliest use date as submission date plus the 45-day CMS review period, and record it on the register row.
For File-and-Use materials compute submission date plus 5 days and record that as the earliest use date.
Set a hold on the material in the marketing workflow that cannot be lifted before the computed date.
Where CMS returns the material as disapproved or requiring change, void the earliest use date and restart the clock on resubmission.
checklist.done: every material carries a computed earliest use date and a system hold that cannot be lifted before it.

checklist.step: Read and act on the CMS disposition for each material
actions: Check the HPMS marketing module daily for status changes against every open Material ID.
Record the disposition — accepted, accepted with changes, or disapproved — with its date on the register row.
For accepted-with-changes, apply the exact CMS-required edits, resubmit and capture the new Material ID before any use.
For disapproved materials, withdraw them from every channel and confirm withdrawal in writing from Marketing, the agency channel and the web team.
checklist.done: each Material ID shows a recorded CMS disposition and disapproved material is evidenced as withdrawn from every channel.

checklist.step: Lock distribution channels until the marketing date
actions: Schedule every contract-year email, direct mail drop and paid campaign with a start date no earlier than October 1 and confirm the scheduler rejects earlier dates.
Set the public plan pages and the plan finder feed to publish on October 1 and confirm no preview URL is publicly reachable before then.
Hold agent-facing kits in the distribution portal behind a date-based entitlement so field staff cannot pull them early.
Take a dated screenshot of each channel's schedule as evidence of the lock.
checklist.done: every channel is scheduled no earlier than October 1 with a captured screenshot proving the lock.

checklist.step: Block enrollment intake before the annual enrollment period opens
actions: Configure the enrollment application to reject any contract-year application with an application date before October 15.
Apply the same rule in the broker portal, the online enrollment page and the contact centre script so no channel can bypass it.
Test the block by attempting a dated application on October 14 in the test environment and evidence the rejection.
Confirm with the contact centre supervisor that agents are scripted to take no enrollment before the open date.
checklist.done: every enrollment channel rejects a pre-October-15 application and the rejection has been tested and evidenced.

checklist.step: Gate the benefit configuration to the January 1 effective date
actions: Load the approved contract-year benefit configuration with an effective date of January 1 and confirm the prior year's configuration remains authoritative until December 31.
Run a claims adjudication test on a December service date and a January service date and prove each picks up the correct year's cost share.
Confirm no configuration record carries an effective date earlier than January 1 for the new contract year.
File the test results with the release record.
checklist.done: the contract-year configuration is effective January 1 only and dual-date adjudication tests prove correct year selection.

checklist.step: Verify prior-authorization policies were committee-reviewed before use
actions: List every prior authorization policy that will be applied in the contract year with its clinical basis and its effective date.
Confirm the utilization management committee reviewed each one within the year, as 42 CFR 422.137(d) requires, and minute the review.
Confirm the continuity-of-care rule under 42 CFR 422.138 is configured so an active course of treatment for a new enrollee is honoured for at least 90 days.
Block go-live for any policy with no committee review record.
checklist.done: no prior authorization policy goes live without a dated UM committee review and the 90-day continuity rule is configured.

checklist.step: Run the pre-release readiness review
actions: Two weeks before October 1, walk the release record for every PBP id and confirm all four gate flags have a named releaser and date or a documented reason they remain blocked.
Check the material register for any material whose earliest use date falls after October 1 and confirm it is excluded from the launch pack.
Confirm the contact centre, broker channel and web team have received only cleared materials.
Record the readiness decision per PBP id — launch, launch partial, or hold.
checklist.done: each PBP id has a minuted readiness decision and no uncleared material sits in the launch pack.

checklist.step: Release the gate and record who authorised it
actions: Lift each gate flag individually, recording the releaser name, the date and time and the evidence relied on — approval date, Material ID and disposition, or the computed earliest use date.
Refuse to lift a flag on verbal assurance; the evidence reference is mandatory on the record.
Notify Marketing, Sales, the contact centre and the web team the moment a flag is lifted, naming what is now permitted.
Keep the flag history so the sequence of releases is reconstructable.
checklist.done: every lifted flag carries a releaser, a timestamp and a named evidence reference, with the history preserved.

checklist.step: Monitor for premature distribution during the launch window
actions: Each business day between the material submissions and October 15, compare campaign send logs and web publish logs against the material register earliest use dates.
Sweep third-party marketing organisation and agency sites for plan materials published early and demand takedown within 24 hours.
Log any early send with the volume, the audience and the material id and escalate the same day.
Keep the daily comparison output as monitoring evidence for the compliance work plan.
checklist.done: a daily send-versus-earliest-use comparison exists for the whole window and every early send is logged and escalated the same day.

checklist.step: Handle any premature use as a breach, not a defect
actions: For each premature distribution, stop the channel immediately and quantify recipients, dates and the material's review status at the time of use.
Assess correction: retraction notice, corrected mailing, or beneficiary-level outreach where a benefit or premium was misstated.
Have Regulatory Counsel decide whether the incident is self-reported to the CMS account manager and record the decision and its basis.
Record the disciplinary step taken under 42 CFR 422.503(b)(4)(vi)(E) where an individual bypassed the gate.
checklist.done: every premature use has a stopped channel, a quantified impact, a correction, a documented self-report decision and a disciplinary record where applicable.

checklist.step: Archive the gate record for the contract year
actions: Assemble the release records with flag histories, the material register with Material IDs and dispositions, the channel schedule screenshots and the enrollment block test into one contract-year record.
Apply the 10-year retention label required by 42 CFR 422.504(d) from the end of the contract year.
Index by H-number, PBP id, Material ID and gate flag.
Verify a test retrieval by Material ID returns the submitted file, the disposition and the distribution date.
checklist.done: the gate record is archived, labelled for 10 years and retrievable by Material ID with file, disposition and distribution date.

testing.step: Build the population of contract-year materials and releases
actions: Export every Material ID recorded in the HPMS Marketing Review Module for the contract year across all H-numbers, with submission date, type and disposition.
Add every release record and gate flag history from the internal system, and every campaign send record from the marketing platform.
Reconcile the three sources and investigate any campaign send with no matching Material ID.
Sign the population as complete with the extract date and extractor name.
testing.done: materials, releases and sends are reconciled to one another and the population is signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile every distributed material to a reviewed Material ID
actions: Match each send or publish event to a Material ID on material name and version.
Confirm the disposition on that Material ID was accepted, or the File-and-Use route applied, at the time of the send.
List any distribution with no Material ID, or with a disapproved Material ID, as an automatic exception.
Confirm the distributed file is byte-identical to the file stored as submitted.
testing.done: every distribution ties to an accepted Material ID with a file identical to the submitted version, or is an exception.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of materials and PBP releases
actions: Take 100% of File-and-Use materials, 100% of disapproved or accepted-with-changes materials and 100% of gate overrides.
Add a seeded random selection of 20 standard-review materials and 10 PBP release records.
Record the seed, population size and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
Note which items are mandatory coverage and which are random.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all File-and-Use, changed and overridden items, and its basis is documented.

testing.step: Re-perform the review-route classification independently
actions: For each sampled material, read the CY marketing requirements and reach your own view on whether it is standard-review, File-and-Use eligible, or a required model document.
Compare to the recorded classification without reading it first, and treat any difference as an exception including a right answer with the wrong basis.
Confirm model and standardised documents were used in CMS's wording without unauthorised edits.
Capture the guidance section relied on into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled material has an independent route conclusion compared to the recorded one, with the guidance section captured.

testing.step: Recompute the review and File-and-Use clocks
actions: For each sampled material recompute earliest use date as submission date plus 45 days for standard review, or plus 5 days for File-and-Use.
Compare the recomputed date to the first actual distribution date read from the campaign send log or web publish log.
Where a resubmission occurred, confirm the clock restarted on the resubmission date and not the original.
Any distribution before the recomputed date is a reportable breach, not a test exception.
testing.done: every sampled material's clock is recomputed and no distribution pre-dates its earliest use date, or the breach is quantified.

testing.step: Test the October 1 and October 15 date locks
actions: Query the campaign and publish logs for any contract-year plan material sent or published before October 1 and list every hit.
Query the enrollment records for any contract-year application with an application date before October 15, across the online, broker and contact centre channels.
Re-run the enrollment block test yourself in the test environment with an October 14 application date and record the system response.
Confirm no channel accepted an application outside the October 15 to December 7 window without a valid special enrollment period reason code.
testing.done: no plan material pre-dates October 1 and no application pre-dates October 15 without a valid special enrollment reason, with the block independently tested.

testing.step: Trace the sampled releases to CMS bid approval evidence
actions: For each sampled PBP release record, open HPMS Contract Management and read the bid approval date directly.
Confirm the bid-approved gate flag was lifted on or after that date and not before.
Compare the benefit and premium values advertised in the sampled materials to the CMS-approved values and list any difference to the cent.
Capture the HPMS approval screen into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled release is proved to follow an HPMS bid approval and advertised values equal approved values.

testing.step: Test the January 1 benefit effective-date gate
actions: Extract the contract-year benefit configuration records and read the effective date on each.
List any record effective before January 1 of the contract year.
Re-run an adjudication test on a December 31 and a January 1 service date and confirm each selects the correct contract year's cost share.
Trace any prior-authorization policy applied in the year to a dated UM committee review under 42 CFR 422.137(d).
testing.done: no benefit configuration is effective before January 1, dual-date adjudication is correct, and every applied prior-authorization policy has a committee review.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception with the Material ID or PBP id, the date breached, the recipient volume and the CMS citation engaged.
Assign a root cause — misclassified route, clock miscomputed, scheduler override, agency site publish, gate lifted without evidence — and an owner.
Set a remediation date and record whether Regulatory Counsel decided to self-report to the CMS account manager.
Carry every open exception into next contract year's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue with quantified impact, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a self-report decision.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report the test
actions: Compute the premature-distribution rate and the pre-window enrollment count and compare both to the zero-tolerance threshold.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with workpaper references.
Have the Internal Auditor, who submitted no sampled material and authorised no sampled release, sign the workpaper.
Report the result and any breach to the compliance committee and file the signed workpaper under the contract year.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the breach counts, the conclusion and the committee reporting date and is filed in the repository.

checklist.step: Baseline the CMS-approved artifacts for the contract year
actions: Download the final approved PBP report and the post-negotiation BPT for every plan ID from HPMS once CMS issues bid approval (typically late summer).
Version-lock the approved set in the Internal Regulatory System as <H#>-<PBP#>-<CY>-APPROVED and mark all earlier drafts superseded.
Diff the approved PBP against the June-submitted version and list every value CMS changed in negotiation.
Hand the locked baseline and the negotiation-change list to the Business Systems Analyst as the sole configuration source.
checklist.done: a version-locked approved baseline and negotiation-change list are published as the single configuration source.

checklist.step: Author field-level configuration requirements traced to the PBP
actions: For each plan ID, write one requirement row per PBP benefit line: benefit category, in/out-of-network cost share, deductible applicability, authorization rule and visit/day limits, citing the PBP section (e.g., Section B-4a inpatient).
Add the plan-level rows: premium, Part B premium buydown, combined/split MOOP amounts and the rebate-funded supplemental benefits.
Trace each row to its target system field in enrollment, claims and billing so nothing is configured from memory.
Have the Product Manager approve the traceability matrix before any build starts.
checklist.done: an approved traceability matrix maps every PBP benefit line to named system fields.

checklist.step: Build the plan-year benefit plans in the enrollment/policy admin system
actions: Create the contract-year benefit plan shells per plan ID with contract number, PBP number, segment and service-area counties from the approved baseline.
Key premium, effective dates (January 1 start) and enrollment-eligibility parameters from the traceability matrix.
Attach the plan crosswalk so renewing members map to the correct successor plan ID.
Peer-review each keyed value against the matrix row and initial the build log.
checklist.done: every plan ID exists in policy admin with premium, dates and crosswalk peer-reviewed against the matrix.

checklist.step: Configure benefit cost sharing in the claims adjudication rules
actions: Build the benefit grid per plan ID in the claims platform: copay/coinsurance per service category, deductible logic, in/out-of-network tiers and benefit limits, keyed only from the traceability matrix.
Map service categories to procedure/revenue code sets with the Medical Claims Reviewer so each PBP category adjudicates against the right codes.
Configure cost-sharing no higher than the approved PBP value in every case — a lower value is a pricing error, a higher value is a member-harm compliance defect.
Record each configured rule id against its matrix row.
checklist.done: claims rules exist for every benefit line with rule ids recorded on the matrix and no value above the approved PBP.

checklist.step: Configure MOOP accumulators and catastrophic protection
actions: Set the in-network and combined maximum out-of-pocket amounts per plan ID exactly as approved in the PBP.
Configure which cost-sharing amounts accrue to each accumulator per the CMS MOOP service-category rules in the bid instructions.
Verify the accumulator zeroes member cost sharing on covered Parts A/B services once the MOOP is reached.
Run three worked examples (below, at, above MOOP) and file the results with the build record.
checklist.done: MOOP accumulators match the approved amounts and the three worked examples behave correctly.

checklist.step: Configure the SNP model-of-care triggers for each SNP plan
actions: From the NCQA-approved model of care, configure the health risk assessment task to trigger within 90 days of each SNP enrollment effective date, per 42 CFR 422.101(f) and the MOC's own committed timeframe.
Configure individualized care plan creation and interdisciplinary care team assignment workflows to follow HRA completion, matching the MOC's stated intervals.
Load the target-population eligibility verification step (e.g., chronic-condition or dual-eligibility check) into the enrollment workflow.
Walk the Medical / Nurse Case Manager through the configured workflow and capture their written confirmation that it matches the approved MOC.
checklist.done: HRA, care-plan and ICT workflows fire on the MOC-committed timeframes, confirmed in writing by care management.

checklist.step: Configure premiums and rebate-funded amounts in billing
actions: Key the member premium, any Part B buydown and late-enrollment-penalty handling per plan ID from the approved BPT/PBP baseline.
Configure premium withhold vs direct-bill options consistent with the plan's CMS election handling.
Reconcile the keyed premium to the PBP report value for every plan ID and attach the reconciliation to the build record.
Have the Billing Operations Manager sign the premium configuration.
checklist.done: billing premiums reconcile to the approved PBP for every plan ID with a signed build record.

checklist.step: Reconcile member materials against the configured benefits
actions: Tick-and-tie the ANOC/EOC benefit tables for each plan ID against the configured claims benefit grid, value by value.
Route any mismatch to the Configuration Engineer (if the build is wrong) or the Communications Specialist (if the material is wrong) before the ANOC mail date.
Record the tie-out result per plan ID in the requirements repository.
Certify materials-to-configuration agreement to the Compliance Officer before October 15.
checklist.done: ANOC/EOC values agree with the configured benefits for every plan ID before the AEP starts.

checklist.step: Build the UAT case library from the approved PBP
actions: Write test cases per plan ID covering every benefit category, both network tiers, deductible interaction, each benefit limit, and MOOP crossover.
Add SNP cases: enrollment of a target-population member, HRA trigger timing, care-plan task creation and an out-of-population rejection.
Add negative cases: a basic Part A/B benefit must never deny for a covered enrollee, per 42 CFR 422.101(a).
Link every case to its traceability-matrix row and load the suite into the test plan.
checklist.done: a traceable UAT suite covers all benefit lines, SNP triggers and negative cases.

checklist.step: Execute UAT and tick-and-tie results to the PBP report
actions: Adjudicate the test claims in the claims test environment and record actual member cost sharing per case.
Compare each result to the approved PBP value on the linked matrix row and mark pass/fail — no tolerance on cost-sharing differences.
Log every fail as a defect with the configured value, the approved value and the rule id.
Publish the pass rate and open-defect list to the Test Lead daily during the UAT window.
checklist.done: every UAT case shows a pass/fail against the approved PBP value with defects logged.

checklist.step: Verify prior-authorization rules do not narrow Medicare coverage
actions: List every prior-authorization and step-therapy rule configured for the plan year and map each to the supporting NCD/LCD or internal coverage policy.
Confirm no rule denies or restricts a service that an applicable NCD/LCD covers, per 42 CFR 422.101(b).
Confirm approved-authorization validity periods meet the CMS minimum and that service-request decision timeframes are configured (14 calendar days standard, 72 hours expedited).
File the rule-by-rule review in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: every configured authorization rule maps to a coverage source and no rule is more restrictive than an NCD/LCD.

checklist.step: Triage defects and gate the release on compliance-relevant fixes
actions: Classify each defect: member-harm (cost share too high, benefit denied), plan-harm (cost share too low), or cosmetic.
Block release on any open member-harm defect; document Product Manager risk acceptance for plan-harm items deferred past January 1.
Retest every fixed defect against its original case and close it with the retest evidence attached.
Publish the release-readiness summary to the Release Coordinator.
checklist.done: zero open member-harm defects and a documented disposition for every other defect.

checklist.step: Approve and deploy the plan-year configuration to production
actions: Raise the change request referencing the UAT sign-off, the traceability matrix version and the approved-baseline id.
Obtain approvals from the Product Manager, Compliance Officer and IT Service Delivery Manager on the change record.
Deploy in the cutover window so the configuration is live and verified before January 1, with a documented rollback plan.
Record deployment evidence (migration logs, smoke-test results) on the change record.
checklist.done: an approved, evidenced change record shows the configuration live before January 1 with rollback documented.

checklist.step: Verify production behaviour in the first weeks of the plan year
actions: Sample the first live claims per plan ID in January and compare adjudicated member cost sharing to the approved PBP values.
Check SNP January enrollments generated HRA tasks with due dates within the MOC-committed 90 days.
Route any discrepancy immediately to the Configuration Engineer and the Compliance Officer with the affected claim/member ids.
Report the verification result to the Product Manager by January 31.
checklist.done: a January production verification confirms claims and SNP triggers match the approved design, or discrepancies are escalated.

checklist.step: Archive the implementation record for 10 years
actions: File the approved baseline, traceability matrix, build records, UAT workbooks, change record and production verification under contract year and plan ID.
Apply the 10-year retention label per 42 CFR 422.504(d).
Verify retrieval by plan ID and contract year in the repository index.
Close the implementation milestone in the release plan.
checklist.done: the complete implementation record is archived with 10-year retention and retrievable by plan ID.

testing.step: Build the population of configured plan IDs and benefit lines
actions: Extract every contract-year benefit plan from the policy admin and claims platforms with its configuration version and deployment date.
Independently list the plan IDs CMS approved from the HPMS approval records in the Internal Regulatory System.
Resolve any plan configured-but-not-approved or approved-but-not-configured before sampling — either is an automatic exception.
testing.done: the configured population reconciles one-for-one to the CMS-approved plan list.

testing.step: Reconcile the traceability matrix to the approved PBP
actions: For each sampled plan, count the PBP benefit lines in the approved report and compare to the matrix row count.
Confirm the matrix cites the APPROVED baseline version, not the June submission, including all negotiation changes.
Flag any PBP line with no matrix row as a coverage gap in the build.
testing.done: every approved PBP line traces to a matrix row built from the correct baseline.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of plans and benefit lines
actions: Take 100% of SNP plan IDs and all plans with negotiation changes.
Randomly select (seeded, reproducible) 20 benefit lines per sampled plan, always including inpatient, MOOP and two supplemental benefits.
Record seed, population and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers all SNPs, negotiated changes and the mandatory benefit lines.

testing.step: Re-perform the configuration comparison against the approved PBP
actions: For each sampled benefit line, read the live production rule value directly from the claims platform without consulting the build log.
Compare to the approved PBP report value; any member cost share above the approved value is a member-harm exception.
Screenshot the production rule and the PBP line into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled line has an independent production-to-PBP comparison with captured evidence.

testing.step: Re-adjudicate test claims through the production configuration
actions: Run a re-adjudication set in the production-mirror environment covering each sampled benefit line and both network tiers.
Independently compute the expected member liability from the PBP values and compare to the system result.
Verify a covered Part A/B basic-benefit test claim cannot deny, per 42 CFR 422.101(a).
testing.done: system-adjudicated liability matches independently computed PBP values on every re-adjudicated claim.

testing.step: Recompute the MOOP accumulator behaviour
actions: Select members near the MOOP from January–February accumulator data and recompute their accrued cost sharing from claim detail.
Verify accrual only includes the MOOP-eligible service categories and that post-MOOP claims paid at zero member liability.
Log any member charged after crossing the approved MOOP as a member-harm exception requiring reprocessing.
testing.done: recomputed accumulators match the system and no post-MOOP member charge exists in the sample.

testing.step: Verify SNP model-of-care triggers fired as approved
actions: Pull all SNP enrollments effective January 1–31 and trace each to an HRA task due within the MOC-committed 90 days, per 42 CFR 422.101(f) and 422.152(g).
Trace completed HRAs to care-plan creation and ICT assignment within the MOC intervals.
List any enrollment with no HRA task as an exception with member id.
testing.done: every sampled SNP enrollment shows timely HRA, care-plan and ICT workflow records.

testing.step: Verify the release gate and deployment evidence
actions: Inspect the change record for the plan-year release and confirm UAT sign-off, the three approvals and the rollback plan pre-date deployment.
Confirm deployment completed before January 1 and that no member-harm defect was open at release.
Trace two fixed defects to retest evidence.
testing.done: the release was approved, evidenced and deployed on time with no open member-harm defects.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception with plan ID, benefit line, configured vs approved value and the member impact.
For member-harm exceptions, open claim reprocessing with member refunds and assess CMS self-disclosure with Regulatory Counsel.
Assign root cause (matrix gap, keying error, missed negotiation change) and an owner with a remediation date.
Carry open items into the 60-day post-implementation retest.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, impact assessment, root cause, owner and remediation date.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the verification
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-member-harm threshold.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer — who built none of the sampled configuration — sign the workpaper and file it in the compliance evidence repository.
Report results and any reprocessing totals to the Compliance Committee within 60 days of January 1.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and reprocessing totals is filed and reported.
