checklist.step: Run the daily HPMS monitoring rota
actions: Each business morning, open HPMS and review the desk-review correspondence threads, the marketing-module status changes and new HPMS memos for every H-contract.
Check the shared regulatory mailbox for CMS account-manager emails and letters that arrive outside HPMS.
Post a daily 'CMS intake' note to the regulatory Teams channel listing every new item found, or 'no new items'.
Name a backup monitor on the rota so no business day goes unmonitored.
checklist.done: a dated intake note exists for every business day and names each new CMS item or states none.

checklist.step: Log each objection and compute its due date at intake
actions: Create a tracker row per CMS item the same day it is found: CMS reference id, H-contract/plan ID, request text verbatim, received date and channel.

Compute the due date from the CMS-stated period (e.g., 72 hours for a desk-review question, 30 days for a corrective response, 60 days of receipt where the letter says so) using calendar vs business days exactly as CMS states them.
Attach the CMS request document or HPMS thread capture to the row.
Set the tracker reminders at 50% elapsed and T-2 business days.
checklist.done: every CMS item has a same-day tracker row with verbatim request text and a computed, evidenced due date.

checklist.step: Classify the objection and assign the accountable owner
actions: Classify each row: bid/pricing (owner Product / Filing Actuary), benefit design (Product Manager), marketing material (Marketing Compliance Analyst), compliance program or conduct (Compliance Officer).
Assign the drafting owner and the clearance path from the procedure's clearance matrix within one business day of intake.
Flag any item that signals a possible deficiency finding and copy Regulatory Counsel immediately.
Confirm the owner has acknowledged the assignment and the due date on the tracker row.
checklist.done: every open item shows a classification, an acknowledged owner and a clearance path within one business day.

checklist.step: Pull the source records the response will rely on
actions: Retrieve the exact filed versions in question — approved PBP report, BPT worksheet, submitted marketing piece or compliance artifact — from the version-locked baseline in the Internal Regulatory System.
Never reconstruct from working copies; the response must quote the filed version CMS is looking at.
Hand the source set to the drafting owner with the CMS request text.
Note the retrieved version ids on the tracker row.
checklist.done: the drafting owner holds the version-locked filed records with version ids noted on the row.

checklist.step: Draft the response answering exactly what CMS asked
actions: Answer each CMS question in the order asked, quoting the question and citing the specific worksheet, PBP section or document page that supports the answer.
For pricing questions, rerun the affected BPT calculation and attach the supporting exhibit rather than describing it.
Where CMS is right and a correction is needed, state the correction plainly and describe the corrected resubmission being prepared — never argue around an actual error.
Keep commitments specific: what will change, in which system or document, by what date.
checklist.done: a draft answers every CMS question with cited support and specific, dated commitments.

checklist.step: Run actuarial peer review on any pricing response
actions: Independently rerun the recomputed figures in the draft against the filed BPT and check consistency with the actuarial memorandum.
Confirm the response does not contradict any certified assumption without flagging the certification impact to the certifying actuary.
Sign the peer-review note on the tracker row.
Return discrepancies to the drafter the same day given the short desk-review clocks.
checklist.done: every pricing response carries a same-cycle peer-review sign-off consistent with the certified bid.

checklist.step: Clear the response through counsel where the matrix requires it
actions: Review every response that concedes an error, commits to corrective action, or responds to a compliance-program inquiry under 42 CFR 422.503(b)(4)(vi).
Check commitments are achievable and consistent with positions taken in other open CMS matters.
Record the clearance decision and any required edits on the tracker row within the clearance window in the procedure.
Escalate to the General Counsel any response that could trigger enforcement exposure.
checklist.done: every matrix-flagged response shows a dated counsel clearance before submission.

checklist.step: Submit the response through the correct CMS channel
actions: Submit desk-review answers in the originating HPMS thread, marketing corrections through the HPMS marketing module, and letter responses to the address/mailbox the CMS letter specifies.
Submit at least one business day before the due date wherever the material is ready — never ride the deadline on a system-dependent upload.
Capture the HPMS confirmation screen or delivery receipt immediately after submission.
Record the submission timestamp on the tracker row.
checklist.done: the response is submitted in the CMS-specified channel with a captured receipt and timestamp on the row.

checklist.step: Escalate any response at risk of missing its deadline
actions: At the 50%-elapsed alert, review progress with the owner; at T-2 business days, take over sequencing personally.
Where the date cannot be met, contact the CMS reviewer through the HPMS thread or the account manager before the due date to request an extension, and record CMS's answer verbatim.
Never let a due date pass silently — a documented extension request before the deadline is the minimum outcome.
Log the escalation and outcome on the tracker row.
checklist.done: no due date passes without either a submitted response or a pre-deadline documented extension request.

checklist.step: Track each objection to CMS disposition and closure
actions: Monitor the HPMS thread for CMS's acceptance, follow-up question or disposition on every submitted response.
Treat a CMS follow-up as a new intake row with its own computed due date, linked to the parent.
Close the row only when CMS confirms acceptance or the underlying filing reaches approved/closed status.
Record the closure evidence (thread capture or disposition notice) on the row.
checklist.done: every row is either open with a live due date or closed with captured CMS disposition evidence.

checklist.step: Propagate conceded corrections into the filed baseline
actions: For every correction committed in a response, create the corrected version in the Internal Regulatory System and link it to the objection row.
Notify the Business Systems Analyst where the correction changes values that downstream configuration or member materials consume.
Verify the corrected resubmission was uploaded to HPMS by the committed date.
Mark the baseline superseded so no one builds from the pre-correction version.
checklist.done: every committed correction exists as a linked, resubmitted baseline version and downstream owners were notified.

checklist.step: Handle marketing-material disapprovals and withdrawals
actions: On an HPMS marketing disapproval, instruct the Marketing Manager the same day to pull the piece from every distribution channel and record the pull time.
Log where the material had already been distributed and assess member impact with the Compliance Officer.
Correct and resubmit the material through the HPMS marketing module, observing the applicable review or File-and-Use period before any redistribution.
File the disapproval, pull evidence and resubmission receipt on the objection row.
checklist.done: disapproved material is pulled same-day, impact is assessed, and the corrected piece cleared review before redistribution.

checklist.step: Review the objection log weekly for aging and risk
actions: Run the weekly aging view: items past 50% elapsed, items at T-2, and anything unacknowledged by its owner.
Challenge any item parked in clearance longer than the procedure allows.
Confirm exceptions (late or missed responses) opened within one business day of the miss.
Minute the review and file it with the log.
checklist.done: a minuted weekly review exists with no unowned or silently aging item.

checklist.step: Trend objection causes into the next filing cycle
actions: Quarterly, categorize closed objections by cause: BPT arithmetic, PBP inconsistency, unsupported benefit, marketing claim, missing compliance element.
Feed the top causes into the next cycle's package-assembly checklist and reviewer focus areas.
Report the trend and repeat-cause count to the Compliance Committee.
Record the resulting checklist changes as evidence the loop closed.
checklist.done: a quarterly cause trend exists and drove documented changes to the next cycle's checklist.

checklist.step: Archive the objection record for 10 years
actions: Move closed objection rows with their request text, cleared responses, receipts and dispositions into the compliance evidence repository under contract year and H-contract.
Apply the 10-year retention label per 42 CFR 422.504(d).
Verify retrieval by CMS reference id and plan ID.
Confirm the tracker row links to the archived record.
checklist.done: every closed objection is archived with 10-year retention and retrievable by CMS reference id.

testing.step: Build the objection population from the CMS side, not the log
actions: Extract every desk-review question, marketing action and memo action item for the period directly from the HPMS threads and modules for each H-contract.
Add CMS letters and account-manager emails from the shared regulatory mailbox.
This HPMS-sourced list is the population — the internal log is the thing being tested, never the source.
testing.done: a CMS-sourced population list exists independent of the internal objection log.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the objection log
actions: Match every population item to a tracker row on CMS reference id and received date.
List any CMS item with no tracker row as an intake-failure exception — these are the most serious finding this test can produce.
Check the tracker received date is the same day as the HPMS posting date for matched items.
testing.done: every CMS item matches a same-day tracker row or is listed as an intake-failure exception.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of objections
actions: Take 100% of items that conceded an error or committed corrective action, and 100% of marketing disapprovals.
Randomly select (seeded, reproducible) 25% of the remainder, minimum 15 items.
Record seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers all concessions and disapprovals plus a random remainder.

testing.step: Recompute every sampled due date from the CMS request text
actions: Read the verbatim CMS request and independently recompute the due date, applying calendar vs business days exactly as CMS stated (72-hour, 14-calendar-day, 30-day and 60-days-of-receipt clocks).
Compare to the tracker's computed due date; a wrong computation is an exception even when the response still landed on time.
Note the recomputation on each sampled row in the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled due date is independently recomputed and compared to the tracker.

testing.step: Verify submission timestamps against receipts in HPMS
actions: Open the HPMS thread or module for each sampled item and read the actual submission timestamp from the CMS side.
Compare to the recomputed due date; any submission after the due date without a pre-deadline documented extension is a fail.
Capture the HPMS timestamp evidence into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled response shows an HPMS-evidenced timestamp on or before its recomputed due date, or a fail is logged.

testing.step: Test the clearance trail on sampled responses
actions: For each sampled pricing response, confirm a Pricing Actuary peer-review sign-off pre-dates submission.
For each concession or corrective commitment, confirm a dated Regulatory Counsel clearance pre-dates submission.
A response submitted before its required clearance is an exception regardless of content quality.
testing.done: every sampled response shows the required sign-offs dated before submission.

testing.step: Trace committed corrections to resubmission and downstream systems
actions: For each sampled commitment, find the corrected baseline version and the HPMS resubmission by the committed date.
Where the correction changed member-facing values, confirm the Business Systems Analyst was notified and the configuration or materials were updated.
An unfulfilled commitment to CMS is a reportable breach, not a test exception.
testing.done: every sampled commitment traces to a dated resubmission and completed downstream updates.

testing.step: Verify marketing disapprovals were pulled and re-cleared
actions: For each sampled disapproval, verify the same-day pull evidence and the distribution-impact assessment.
Confirm the corrected material completed its HPMS review or File-and-Use period before any redistribution.
Any redistribution before clearance is a reportable marketing violation.
testing.done: every sampled disapproval shows same-day pull, impact assessment and pre-clearance before redistribution.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception with the CMS reference id, what failed (intake, computation, timeliness, clearance, commitment) and the impact.
Assign root cause (monitoring gap, wrong day-count basis, clearance bottleneck, owner overload) and an owner.
Set a remediation date; intake failures also trigger a monitoring-rota redesign.
Carry open exceptions into the next semi-annual test as mandatory retests.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute on-time percentage against the 98% threshold and count intake failures against the zero tolerance.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer — who drafted or cleared none of the sampled responses — sign the workpaper and file it in the compliance evidence repository.
Report results and any unfulfilled CMS commitments to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and threshold comparison is filed and reported.

checklist.step: Maintain the record-class catalog for MA filing records
actions: Keep a catalog row per record class: bid package (PBP/BPT/actuarial certification), CMS approval letters, HPMS submission receipts, desk-review threads, marketing approvals and File-and-Use attestations, objection responses and closures.
For each class state the trigger event, the capture owner, the naming pattern <H#>-<PBP#>-<CY>-<class>-<date> and the 10-year retention rule from 42 CFR 422.504(d).
Review the catalog annually against the current CMS program-audit protocol so every universe CMS can request maps to a class.
Publish the catalog to every filing-team member.
checklist.done: a published catalog covers every record class with trigger, owner, naming and retention, reviewed within 12 months.

checklist.step: Capture each filing event's record set at closure
actions: Within 10 business days of a filing event closing (approval received, objection closed, material cleared), pull the final versions from the Internal Regulatory System and the HPMS captures from the tracker row.
Store them in the repository under contract year → H-contract → plan ID → record class, using the catalog naming pattern.
Record the capture date and source ids in the capture log.
Reject partial sets — an approval without its submitted version and receipt is not a captured event.
checklist.done: every closed filing event has a complete, catalog-named record set in the repository within 10 business days.

checklist.step: Preserve the filed version exactly as submitted
actions: Archive the byte-identical file that went to CMS — the exported PBP upload files, the validated BPT workbook and the submitted PDFs — never a regenerated copy.
Compute and store a checksum for each archived file at capture time.
Where CMS negotiation changed a version, archive both the submitted and the approved versions with a link note explaining the difference.
Mark archived items read-only.
checklist.done: archived files are byte-identical submissions with stored checksums and read-only protection.

checklist.step: Apply the 10-year retention label at capture
actions: Stamp every captured record with a retention end date of 10 years from the end of the relevant contract period per 42 CFR 422.504(d).
Configure the repository so labelled records cannot be deleted or edited before the end date by any user, including administrators.
Verify the label on a spot-check of five records after each monthly capture cycle.
Log label corrections in the capture log.
checklist.done: every archived record carries an enforced 10-year retention label verified by monthly spot-checks.

checklist.step: Overlay legal and audit holds on affected records
actions: On any CMS audit notice, OIG inquiry or litigation touching an H-contract, define the hold scope by contract, plan ID and year range.
Instruct the Records Manager to apply the hold flag, which suspends disposal eligibility regardless of the retention end date.
Keep a hold register with matter name, scope, applied date and release conditions.
Review open holds quarterly and release in writing only when the matter closes.
checklist.done: a current hold register exists and every in-scope record carries an active hold flag until written release.

checklist.step: Control access to the filing archive
actions: Grant read access to the filing, compliance and legal teams by role; restrict write to the named capture custodians; no delete rights for anyone on labelled records.
Recertify the access list quarterly with the Records Manager as reviewer.
Enable access-event logging on the repository folders holding the archive.
Remove leaver access within the joiner-mover-leaver SLA and evidence it.
checklist.done: access follows the role model, is recertified quarterly and access events are logged.

checklist.step: Run the monthly capture-completeness sweep
actions: List every filing event closed in the month from the tracker and the Internal Regulatory System.
Match each to a complete archived record set and its capture-log entry.
Raise a tracker exception for any event with no archive or a partial set, due for cure within 10 business days.
File the sweep result with the capture log.
checklist.done: a monthly sweep result exists showing every closed event archived or excepted with a cure date.

checklist.step: Verify archive integrity annually with checksum re-runs
actions: Re-compute checksums on a 10% random sample of archived files plus every file touched by a migration during the year.
Compare to the capture-time checksums; investigate any mismatch as a potential integrity incident with the Document Management Specialist.
Confirm files in superseded formats still open, and plan format migration where they do not.
File the fixity report with the annual records review.
checklist.done: an annual fixity report shows sampled checksums match capture values or incidents are opened.

checklist.step: Prove the regulator retrieval SLA with drills
actions: Twice a year, have the Compliance Officer name a surprise request mimicking a CMS program-audit universe: e.g., 'the approved PBP, BPT and approval letter for plan <H#-PBP#> for contract year N-3'.
Retrieve the full set and measure elapsed time against the 5-business-day SLA.
Log the drill result and fix any index gap the drill exposes.
Report drill outcomes at the annual records review.
checklist.done: two dated drill results per year show retrieval inside the SLA or fixes for exposed gaps.

checklist.step: Capture marketing approvals with their review-period evidence
actions: For each marketing material, archive the submitted piece, the HPMS material id, the review outcome or File-and-Use attestation, and the date distribution began.
Show on the record that distribution started only after the applicable review or File-and-Use period was satisfied.
Archive withdrawal/pull evidence for any disapproved material alongside the corrected resubmission.
Index by material id and plan year.
checklist.done: every marketing material's archive shows submission, disposition and a compliant distribution start date.

checklist.step: Archive delegated-entity filing records the plan relies on
actions: Identify first-tier/downstream entities that prepare or hold records supporting the plan's filings (e.g., a delegated marketing vendor's distribution logs).
Confirm each contract passes through the 10-year retention and CMS access obligations of 42 CFR 422.504(i).
Obtain an annual attestation from each entity that the records exist and are retrievable, and file it in the repository.
Escalate any refusal or failed attestation to the Compliance Officer.
checklist.done: every relying delegated entity has a contract with pass-through retention terms and a current attestation on file.

checklist.step: Manage migrations without breaking the archive
actions: Before any repository migration or upgrade, export the index and checksums as the pre-migration baseline.
Migrate with retention labels, hold flags and audit trails intact — a migration that strips labels is a compliance incident.
Re-run checksums on migrated content against the baseline and reconcile counts.
Have the Records Manager sign the migration reconciliation.
checklist.done: a signed migration reconciliation shows counts, checksums, labels and holds survived intact.

checklist.step: Run defensible disposal only after retention and holds clear
actions: Generate the annual disposal-eligibility report: records past their 10-year end date with no active hold.
Route the batch to Regulatory Counsel, who checks the hold register and releases the batch in writing.
Dispose via the repository's audited destruction function and retain the destruction certificate.
Never bulk-delete outside this workflow.
checklist.done: disposals happen only from counsel-released batches with destruction certificates on file.

checklist.step: Review the retention program annually with governance
actions: Present the annual records review to the Head of Compliance: sweep results, fixity report, drill outcomes, hold register, disposal certificates and open exceptions.
Update the procedure for any CMS rule or audit-protocol change identified in the year.
Minute decisions and assign owners to improvement actions.
File the review pack in the repository.
checklist.done: a minuted annual review pack exists with assigned improvement actions.

checklist.step: Log and cure every archive exception
actions: Raise a tracker issue for each capture gap, integrity mismatch, failed drill or premature-disposal near-miss with root cause and owner.
Cure capture gaps by locating and archiving the missing record; where it is genuinely lost, document the loss memo with counsel.
Have Regulatory Counsel sign off each cure.
Track exception counts as a monthly metric to the Compliance Manager.
checklist.done: every exception has an issue, a counsel-signed cure or loss memo, and feeds the monthly metric.

testing.step: Build the filing-event population from source systems
actions: List every filing event closed in the tested year from HPMS (submissions, approvals, marketing dispositions) and the Internal Regulatory System — never from the archive being tested.
Include objection closures from the tracker as their own events.
Sign the population as complete with its source extract dates.
testing.done: a source-system population of closed filing events exists independent of the archive.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the archive and capture log
actions: Match every population event to a complete archived record set and a capture-log entry.
Check the capture date fell within 10 business days of event closure.
List unmatched events and late captures as exceptions.
testing.done: every event matches a timely, complete archive entry or is listed as an exception.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of archived record sets
actions: Take 100% of bid-package and CMS-approval record sets, plus all records under an active hold.
Randomly select (seeded, reproducible) 20 further record sets across marketing and objection classes.
Record seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers all bid/approval sets, held records and a random remainder.

testing.step: Re-perform retrieval within the regulator SLA
actions: Request each sampled set from the Records Manager using only contract number, plan ID and contract year, as CMS would.
Measure elapsed time against the 5-business-day SLA and completeness against the record-class catalog.
Log any set that cannot be produced complete and on time.
testing.done: every sampled set was retrieved complete within the SLA or logged as a fail.

testing.step: Verify archived files are the versions CMS actually received
actions: For sampled bid records, compare the archived PBP/BPT files' checksums to the capture-time checksums and the HPMS submission ids on the receipts.
For sampled approvals, match the approval letter's referenced version to the archived submitted version.
An archived regenerated copy in place of the submitted original is an integrity exception.
testing.done: sampled archives are checksum-verified originals matching the HPMS submission ids.

testing.step: Test retention labels and immutability
actions: Read the retention end date on each sampled record and recompute 10 years from the end of the relevant contract period per 42 CFR 422.504(d).
Attempt an edit and a delete on one sampled record under a test account with custodian rights and confirm both are blocked.
Log any record whose label is short-dated or editable.
testing.done: sampled labels recompute correctly and labelled records resist edit and delete.

testing.step: Test holds and the disposal workflow
actions: Trace every record on the hold register to an applied hold flag, and inspect the year's disposal batches for counsel release signatures and destruction certificates.
Search disposed-item logs for any record destroyed inside its 10-year period or while flagged — either is a reportable breach.
Verify at least one disposal batch was checked against the hold register before release.
testing.done: holds trace to flags, disposals trace to counsel releases, and no in-period destruction exists.

testing.step: Verify delegated-entity retention attestations
actions: For each relying delegated entity, inspect the contract clause passing through 42 CFR 422.504(i) retention/access obligations and the current-year attestation.
Request one sample record from one entity through the Vendor Manager and time the response.
List entities with missing clauses or failed attestations as exceptions.
testing.done: every relying entity shows the contract clause, a current attestation and a successful sample retrieval.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception with record class, event id, what failed and the audit-readiness impact.
Assign root cause (capture miss, index gap, label error, migration defect, vendor gap) and an owner.
Set remediation dates; premature destruction also triggers a counsel-led disclosure assessment.
Carry open exceptions into next year's test as mandatory retests.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute capture completeness, retrieval SLA performance and integrity results against the 100% thresholds.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer — who administers no part of the repository — sign the workpaper and file it in the compliance evidence repository.
Report results to the Compliance Committee and fold findings into the annual records review.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion is filed and reported to governance.

checklist.step: Define and maintain the screening population sources
actions: Pull the monthly population extract: all active employees, board members and contingent workers from the HRIS with full legal name, DOB and any prior names.
Pull all first-tier, downstream and related entities from the vendor register with entity name, TIN and key principals per 42 CFR 422.504(i).
Pull the contracted provider and prescriber file (NPI, name, TIN) from the provider data feed for preclusion-list checks.
Reconcile each extract's count to its source system and log the counts in the batch record.
checklist.done: monthly extracts for staff, FDRs and providers exist with counts reconciled to source systems.

checklist.step: Refresh the exclusion and sanctions lists on their publication cycles
actions: Download the updated OIG LEIE database file from oig.hhs.gov/exclusions the week OIG publishes it each month and load it into the screening engine.
Load the SAM.gov exclusions extract and the OFAC SDN and consolidated lists from treasury.gov/ofac on their update cycles.
Load the monthly CMS preclusion list file received through the plan's CMS data channel.
Record each list's version/publication date in the batch record — screening against a stale list invalidates the month.
checklist.done: the engine shows current LEIE, SAM, OFAC and preclusion list versions with load dates in the batch record.

checklist.step: Calibrate matching rules and thresholds
actions: Set fuzzy-match thresholds for name variants, transpositions and aliases, with DOB/TIN as secondary discriminators, and document the settings.
Test any threshold change against a seeded file of known excluded names before promoting it — every seeded name must alert.
Review threshold performance annually using the year's true-match and false-positive rates.
Keep the settings history so any month's matching logic can be reproduced.
checklist.done: documented thresholds pass the seeded-name test and their history is reproducible per month.

checklist.step: Screen every new hire and new contract before start
actions: Wire the pre-hire check into the recruiting workflow so an offer cannot reach start date without a clear screening result against LEIE, SAM and OFAC.
Wire the pre-contract check into vendor onboarding so no FDR contract is executed before its entity and principals screen clear.
Return any potential match to the two-level adjudication before the person starts or the contract signs.
File the pre-start clearance evidence on the HR or vendor record.
checklist.done: no start date or contract execution occurs without filed pre-start clearance evidence.

checklist.step: Run the monthly screening batch for all populations
actions: Execute the batch against the refreshed lists by the 5th business day each month, covering staff, board, temps, FDR entities and principals per 42 CFR 422.503(b)(4)(vi)(F).
Verify the batch processed the full reconciled population count — a short batch is a failed batch.
Export the run log (population count, list versions, alert count, run date) into the batch record.
Notify the Financial Crime AML Officer of completion and alert volume.
checklist.done: a complete monthly batch ran by the 5th business day with a filed run log matching the population count.

checklist.step: Adjudicate alerts through two independent levels
actions: Level 1: compare the alert's name, DOB, TIN/NPI and address against the list entry and disposition as false positive or potential match with written rationale, within 5 business days.
Level 2: the Financial Crime AML Officer reviews every potential match and any false positive on a board member or FDR principal.
Never let the person's manager or the vendor's relationship owner adjudicate their own alert.
Record both levels' dispositions and timestamps in the case record.
checklist.done: every alert shows a two-level, rationale-backed disposition within the 5-business-day SLA.

checklist.step: Act on confirmed exclusion matches immediately
actions: On a confirmed LEIE/SAM match, remove the person from all Medicare-funded work the same day — suspend system access to MA processes with the Access Management Analyst and notify HR for employment action.
For an excluded FDR or principal, suspend the contract's Medicare-related services and invoke the contract's exclusion clause with the Vendor Manager.
Quantify any federal-program payments made during the exclusion period with the Controller for repayment assessment.
Open a counsel-led assessment of OIG self-disclosure under the OIG protocol and minute the decision.
checklist.done: same-day removal is evidenced, exposure is quantified, and a minuted self-disclosure decision exists.

checklist.step: Execute OFAC blocking, rejection and reporting on sanctions matches
actions: On a confirmed SDN match, block the property or reject the transaction as OFAC rules require and freeze any pending payment with Treasury operations.
File the blocked-property or rejected-transaction report to OFAC within 10 business days via the OFAC Reporting System.
Include blocked property in the annual report to OFAC due by September 30.
Keep full records of the blocking action for the 31 CFR 501.601 retention period within the 10-year archive.
checklist.done: blocking/rejection is executed, the 10-business-day OFAC report is filed, and records are archived.

checklist.step: Enforce the preclusion list in claims payment
actions: Load each monthly CMS preclusion list into the claims platform so claims from precluded providers deny from the CMS-stated effective date per 42 CFR 422.222.
Configure the member-protection handling CMS requires, including the applicable advance notice to affected enrollees and hold-harmless for member cost sharing.
Verify with a test claim that a precluded NPI denies with the correct reason code.
Log the load date and test result in the batch record.
checklist.done: the current preclusion list is live in claims with a passing test denial and logged load evidence.

checklist.step: Collect FDR screening attestations and spot-check them
actions: Obtain an annual attestation from each first-tier entity that it screens its own employees and downstream entities monthly against LEIE and SAM, as the FDR oversight duty in 42 CFR 422.504(i) requires.
Spot-check two FDRs per year by requesting a sample month's screening log through the audit clause.
Escalate any FDR that cannot evidence monthly screening to the Compliance Officer for corrective action or termination.
File attestations and spot-check results in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: current attestations exist for every FDR and two spot-checks per year are on file.

checklist.step: Handle screening of board members and temporary staff explicitly
actions: Confirm the monthly population extract includes board members (from the Corporate Secretary's register) and agency temps (from the contingent-worker feed) — the two groups most often missed.
Screen new board appointees before their first meeting and temps before their first day.
Reconcile the board register and temp roster to the batch population each month.
Note the reconciliation in the batch record.
checklist.done: board and temp rosters reconcile into every monthly batch with pre-start screening evidenced.

checklist.step: Monitor batch and alert SLAs with a monthly dashboard
actions: Publish a monthly dashboard: batch completion date vs the 5th-business-day target, population coverage %, alert volume, aging vs the adjudication SLA and open true-match cases.
Flag any red metric to the Financial Crime AML Officer and Compliance Officer the day the dashboard publishes.
Keep the dashboard extracts as evidence for the quarterly test.
Review threshold-worthy trends (rising false positives, aging alerts) at the monthly compliance operations meeting.
checklist.done: a monthly dashboard is published, red metrics are escalated same-day, and extracts are retained.

checklist.step: Train staff who touch screening decisions
actions: Assign annual exclusion/sanctions training to the screening team, HR recruiters, vendor managers and claims configuration staff, covering LEIE, SAM, OFAC and preclusion handling.
Track completion in the LMS and chase non-completers to 100% within the assignment window.
Refresh the course whenever CMS or OFAC guidance changes the procedure.
Export the completion report to the compliance evidence repository annually.
checklist.done: 100% completion is evidenced for the assigned population with the current-year course version.

checklist.step: Log and cure every screening exception
actions: Raise a tracker issue for any missed population member, late batch, aged alert or stale list month, with root cause and owner.
For a missed member, run a catch-up screen immediately and check the missed months retroactively against the lists as they stood.
Have the Compliance Officer sign off each cure, including any retroactive true match's remediation.
Feed exception counts into the monthly dashboard.
checklist.done: every exception has an issue, a completed catch-up screen where relevant, and a signed cure.

checklist.step: Archive the screening evidence for 10 years
actions: File monthly batch records (run logs, list versions, reconciliations), alert case files, true-match remediation packs, OFAC reports and FDR attestations by month and year.
Apply the 10-year retention label per 42 CFR 422.504(d).
Verify a sample month retrieves completely by month and population type.
Confirm OFAC case records also satisfy the 31 CFR 501.601 retention requirement.
checklist.done: monthly screening evidence is archived under 10-year labels and retrievable by month.

testing.step: Build the should-have-been-screened population independently
actions: Extract all persons active at any point in each tested month directly from the HRIS, the board register and the contingent-worker feed.
Extract all active FDR entities and principals from the vendor register and the contracted provider file for the same months.
This independent extract is the test population — the screening batch files are the thing under test.
testing.done: an independent monthly population exists per group, sourced outside the screening system.

testing.step: Reconcile each monthly batch to the independent population
actions: Compare each month's batch input file to the independent population and list every person or entity absent from the batch.
Verify the batch ran by the 5th business day and used that month's LEIE, SAM, OFAC and preclusion list versions.
Any unscreened member or stale-list month is an automatic exception.
testing.done: every monthly batch reconciles to the independent population with current list versions, or exceptions are listed.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of members and alerts
actions: Take 100% of true-match cases, all board members and a random (seeded, reproducible) 25 staff and 10 FDR entities per quarter.
Sample 25 adjudicated alerts across the quarter's months.
Record seed, population sizes and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers all true matches, board members and a random remainder of members and alerts.

testing.step: Re-screen the sample against the period lists
actions: Re-run the sampled names through the engine against the archived list versions for the tested months, using the documented thresholds.
Compare results to the original batch output; a hit the batch missed is a matching-logic exception requiring immediate live re-screen.
Manually check three sampled names directly on the OIG online LEIE search and the OFAC sanctions search as an engine-independent control.
testing.done: re-screening reproduces the batch results, and the manual checks agree, or exceptions are opened.

testing.step: Re-perform adjudication on sampled alerts
actions: Read each sampled alert's list entry and the member's identifiers, and reach an independent match/no-match conclusion before reading the analyst's rationale.
Compare conclusions; a disagreement on a cleared alert escalates to the Financial Crime AML Officer for immediate re-review.
Recompute alert age from creation to level-2 disposition against the 5-business-day SLA.
testing.done: every sampled alert has an independent re-adjudication and a recomputed SLA result.

testing.step: Trace true matches to removal and remediation evidence
actions: For each true match, verify same-day removal from Medicare-funded work: access suspension logs, HR action records or FDR contract suspension notices.
Verify the payment-exposure quantification and the minuted self-disclosure decision with counsel involvement.
Check any excluded party's exposure period against payroll or accounts-payable records for missed payments.
testing.done: every true match traces to same-day removal, quantified exposure and a minuted disclosure decision.

testing.step: Test preclusion enforcement in paid claims
actions: Join the quarter's paid-claims extract to the period preclusion lists on NPI/TIN and list any paid claim from a precluded provider on or after its effective date per 42 CFR 422.222.
Verify the monthly list load dates in the claims platform against the CMS distribution dates.
Any paid precluded claim is a reportable breach requiring recovery and member cost-sharing refund.
testing.done: the paid-claims join shows zero precluded payments, or breaches are escalated with recovery actions.

testing.step: Verify OFAC reporting deadlines were met
actions: For each blocking or rejection in the period, recompute the 10-business-day clock from the action date to the OFAC report submission evidence.
Confirm the annual blocked-property report was filed by September 30 where blocked property existed.
Late OFAC reports are exceptions with counsel notification.
testing.done: every OFAC action traces to an on-time report, or late filings are logged with counsel notified.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception with member/entity id, month, what failed and the program impact.
Assign root cause (feed gap, threshold miss, adjudication error, load delay) and an owner with a remediation date.
For any excluded-party payment or precluded claim, open recovery and the OIG/CMS disclosure assessment.
Carry open exceptions into next quarter's test as mandatory retests.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and any required disclosure assessment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute coverage %, SLA performance and breach counts against the 100%/zero thresholds.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer — who ran or adjudicated no tested batch — sign the workpaper and file it in the compliance evidence repository.
Report results, breaches and recovery totals to the Compliance Committee quarterly.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and threshold results is filed and reported.

checklist.step: Re-confirm the covered-product scope for the enterprise

File the signed covered-product register with the program documents.

checklist.step: Refresh the enterprise AML risk assessment

Include MA-specific money-movement risks: premium refund redirection, provider kickback flows and agent premium theft.
Have the Enterprise Risk Manager challenge the scoring and record the challenge outcome.
checklist.done: a challenged, dated risk assessment exists with actions against every high-residual risk.

checklist.step: Update the written AML program and version it
actions: Revise the program document for the year's risk assessment results, FinCEN guidance changes and independent-testing findings.
Confirm the four pillars are each current: internal controls, designated officer, training, independent testing, per 31 CFR 1025.210(b).
Version the document in the repository with a change log naming what moved and why.
Obtain the Compliance Officer's approval signature on the new version.
checklist.done: an approved, versioned program document reflects the current year's risks and findings.

checklist.step: Confirm the designated officer appointment and board notification
actions: Confirm the designation letter names the current Financial Crime AML Officer with the mandate, authority and resources required by 31 CFR 1025.210(b)(2).
On any incumbency change, issue a new designation letter within 30 days and notify the board audit committee at its next sitting.
Present the annual AML report (program state, SAR volumes, findings) to the audit committee and minute the acknowledgment via the board portal.
File the designation letter and minutes with the program documents.
checklist.done: a current designation letter and minuted board acknowledgment exist for the year.

checklist.step: Define the training population and assign the annual curriculum
actions: Build the training population with the Financial Crime AML Officer: covered-product operations, claims and premium finance staff, agents where required, the screening team and senior management.
Assign the annual AML course (red flags, SAR referral duty, no-tipping-off, OFAC basics) with a completion window of 60 days.
Auto-assign the course to joiners in the population within 30 days of start.
Chase non-completers weekly and escalate at 100% of the window to line management.
checklist.done: the defined population carries a current-year assignment with joiner auto-assignment active.

checklist.step: Evidence training completion to threshold
actions: Export the completion report at window close and compute the completion rate against the ≥95% threshold.
List non-completers with their managers and the escalation actions taken.
File the report and escalation evidence with the program documents.
Feed persistent non-completion into the compliance scorecard.
checklist.done: a filed completion report shows ≥95% or documented escalations for the shortfall.

checklist.step: Calibrate transaction monitoring rules annually
actions: Review each Actimize rule's alert volume, true-positive rate and SAR conversion for the year.
Tune thresholds where false positives drown analysts or where a typology from the risk assessment has no covering rule, testing changes on historical data before promotion.
Document every rule change with rationale and approval in the model governance record.
Verify data feeds into Actimize (premium, refunds, agent commissions) reconcile to source-system counts monthly.
checklist.done: every rule shows an annual calibration record and feeds reconcile monthly.

checklist.step: Run SAR decisioning on escalated cases
actions: Investigate each escalated case in Actimize: transaction history, customer profile, related parties and prior SARs, documenting findings in the case file.
Present file/no-file recommendations to the Financial Crime AML Officer, who makes the SAR decision and records the rationale — no-file rationales are documented as thoroughly as filings.
Start the 30-calendar-day filing clock at the initial-detection date recorded on the case, not the decision date.
Restrict case access to the SAR enclave group.
checklist.done: every escalated case shows a documented investigation and a dated, rationale-backed SAR decision.

checklist.step: File SARs in the FinCEN BSA E-Filing System within the deadline
actions: In the FinCEN BSA E-Filing System open Reports ▸ FinCEN SAR, complete Parts I–V including the Part V narrative describing who, what, when, where and why, and submit.
File within 30 calendar days of initial detection, or 60 days where no subject was identified at detection, per 31 CFR 1025.320.
Save the BSA E-Filing acknowledgment and BSA Identifier into the restricted case file.
For continuing activity, file continuing SARs on the 120-day review cycle.
checklist.done: each SAR shows an acknowledgment with a BSA Identifier filed inside the computed deadline.

checklist.step: Enforce SAR confidentiality and no-tipping-off
actions: Keep SARs and their existence in the restricted enclave — never in general case notes, board packs name aggregate counts only.
Brief any employee subpoenaed about a SAR to route the request to Regulatory Counsel, who handles it under the SAR rules.
Verify enclave access quarterly with the Access Management Analyst.
Log and investigate any suspected disclosure immediately with counsel.
checklist.done: SAR access is enclave-restricted, verified quarterly, and no disclosure incident is unaddressed.

checklist.step: Operate 314(a) and 314(b) information sharing
actions: Download each FinCEN 314(a) request list from the secure portal, search customer and transaction records for the named subjects, and return positive matches within FinCEN's stated deadline (typically 14 days).
Maintain the 314(b) registration where the program uses voluntary sharing, and document each exchange under the safe harbor.
Log every 314(a) cycle with search scope, run date and result.
Keep 314(a) lists confidential and destroy them per FinCEN instructions.
checklist.done: every 314(a) cycle shows an on-time, logged search and any 314(b) exchange is documented.

checklist.step: Integrate OFAC screening outcomes into the AML program
actions: Feed confirmed OFAC matches and blocking actions from the screening program into Actimize case review for SAR consideration.
Cross-reference SAR subjects against the SDN list at decision time.
Reference the screening program's batch evidence in the AML program document rather than duplicating it.
Reconcile quarterly that every blocking action has a corresponding AML case review.
checklist.done: OFAC actions flow into AML case review with a quarterly reconciliation on file.

checklist.step: Commission the annual independent test
actions: Scope the test to all four pillars plus SAR timeliness, 314(a) handling and monitoring-rule governance, per the testing charter and 31 CFR 1025.210(b)(4).
Staff it outside the AML officer's reporting line — internal audit or a qualified external firm.
Complete fieldwork and issue the report within 12 months of the prior test.
Deliver findings with severity ratings and management responses to the Compliance Officer and audit committee.
checklist.done: an independent test report issued within the annual window covers all pillars with rated findings.

checklist.step: Remediate findings on committed dates
actions: Load every finding into the tracker with owner, severity and committed date from the management response.
Review progress monthly and escalate slipping high-severity items to the Compliance Officer.
Evidence each closure (updated procedure, retested rule, refiled training) on the tracker item before closing.
Report open-finding aging to the audit committee at each sitting.
checklist.done: every finding is tracked to an evidenced closure or an escalated, re-committed date.

checklist.step: Archive the program evidence with the correct retention split
actions: File program versions, risk assessments, designation letters, board minutes, training reports and test reports under 10-year labels in the repository.
Hold SARs and supporting documentation in the restricted enclave for 5 years from filing per 31 CFR 1025.320, access-controlled separately.
Verify a sample retrieval of each record class annually.
Log the archive completeness check with the annual review.
checklist.done: program records carry 10-year labels, SAR records sit in the 5-year enclave, and a retrieval check passed.

testing.step: Build the program-element population for the tested year
actions: List the required elements from 31 CFR 1025.210: written program version, risk assessment, officer designation, training cycle, independent test, plus the SAR and 314(a) workflows.
Pull the year's Actimize alert and case extract, the FinCEN BSA E-Filing acknowledgment list from the enclave, and the LMS assignment export.
Sign the population sources and extract dates into the workpaper.
testing.done: a signed population covers every program element with source extracts.

testing.step: Reconcile SAR cases to FinCEN acknowledgments
actions: Match every filed-SAR decision in Actimize to a BSA E-Filing acknowledgment with a BSA Identifier.
Match every acknowledgment back to a decisioned case — an acknowledgment with no case file is as serious as a case with no filing.
List unmatched items in either direction as exceptions.
testing.done: SAR decisions and FinCEN acknowledgments reconcile both ways or exceptions are listed.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of cases, SARs and trainees
actions: Take 100% of filed SARs and all no-file decisions on cases that reached the AML officer.
Randomly select (seeded, reproducible) 20 closed alerts below the escalation line and 25 members of the training population.
Record seed, population sizes and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers all SARs, all officer no-files and random alerts and trainees.

testing.step: Recompute the SAR deadline on every sampled filing
actions: Read the initial-detection date from each case file and recompute 30 calendar days (or 60 where no subject was identified) per 31 CFR 1025.320.
Compare to the BSA E-Filing submission timestamp on the acknowledgment.
Any late filing is a fail with the day-count shown; check continuing-activity SARs hit the 120-day cycle.
testing.done: every sampled SAR shows a recomputed deadline met, or fails are logged with day counts.

testing.step: Re-perform the file/no-file judgement on sampled cases
actions: Read each sampled case's transaction history and evidence in Actimize and reach an independent file/no-file view before reading the officer's rationale.
Escalate any disagreement on a no-file to the Compliance Officer for a fresh decision with a new detection-date assessment.
Check below-line closed alerts for patterns that should have escalated.
testing.done: every sampled decision has an independent re-performance and disagreements were re-decided.

testing.step: Verify the officer designation and board reporting
actions: Inspect the designation letter's date, mandate and signature and confirm it covers the whole tested year without a gap on incumbency change.
Trace the annual AML report to audit-committee minutes in the board portal.
A designation gap or missing board acknowledgment is a program-element fail.
testing.done: the designation and board acknowledgment cover the full year without gaps.

testing.step: Verify training completion against the defined population
actions: Independently rebuild the training population from HR data using the program's population definition and compare to the LMS assignment.
Recompute the completion rate against the ≥95% threshold and verify sampled completion certificates exist.
Check three joiners were auto-assigned within 30 days of start.
testing.done: the rebuilt population matches the assignment, the threshold is met, and joiner assignment works.

testing.step: Test 314(a) timeliness and monitoring-rule governance
actions: For each 314(a) cycle in the year, compare the search-and-response log dates to FinCEN's stated deadline.
Inspect two Actimize rule changes for documented rationale, pre-promotion testing and approval in the model governance record.
Verify the monthly feed reconciliations ran for the sampled months.
testing.done: all 314(a) cycles were on time and sampled rule changes show governed, tested promotion.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception naming the pillar, what failed and the regulatory exposure.
Assign root cause (clock started late, population gap, governance skip) and an owner with a remediation date.
For late SARs, document the cure and the decision on proactive FinCEN contact taken with Regulatory Counsel.
Carry open exceptions into the next annual test as mandatory retests.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and any counsel-cleared cure.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the independent test
actions: Compute results against the thresholds: program elements current, SAR timeliness, ≥95% training, on-time 314(a).
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer — organizationally separate from the AML officer's line per 31 CFR 1025.210(b)(4) — sign the report.
File the report in the compliance evidence repository and present it to the Compliance Officer and audit committee with management responses.
testing.done: a signed independent-test report with a stated conclusion is filed and presented to governance.
